company_or_scope: Any multinational employer with EU headcount
observed_fact: Only 4 of 27 EU member states (Italy, Lithuania, Malta, Slovakia) met the 7 June 2026 transposition deadline for the EU Pay Transparency Directive. First gender pay gap reports are due 2027 to 2028 depending on employer size.
inference: Employers with EU operations likely do not yet have a working gender pay gap reporting process in place, since most member states have not finalized the implementing rules they would report against.
unknown: Which specific companies are behind on this. Not named here.

observed_fact: A US Magistrate Judge granted final approval on 11 June 2026 of a 50 million dollar settlement covering more than 4,000 current and former Black Google employees, resolving claims the company systematically underpaid and under-promoted them. Google also agreed to three years of pay equity review reforms.
inference: Even a company with mature HR systems and heavy prior scrutiny still needed a court-ordered pay equity review process, this is the ceiling case for why a continuous governance layer matters.
unknown: Nothing material, this fact is well documented with a named court order.

observed_fact: An IHOP franchise operator with several Washington locations agreed to a 6.3 million dollar settlement in 2025 resolving claims it did not disclose wage scales and salary ranges in job postings, violating Washington state law.
inference: Multi-location employers that post jobs in Washington without salary ranges carry comparable exposure.
unknown: Exact settlement date, franchise operator's legal name.

observed_fact: A California court approved a 43 million dollar settlement in 2025 resolving gender pay discrimination claims against Disney, where plaintiffs alleged female employees were paid less than male counterparts in comparable roles.
inference: Companies with no real-time pay governance layer keep landing in settlements of this size, this is a pattern, not an isolated case.
